newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OVERNIGHT GUILDERS STEADY TO FIRM AFTER RECENT DIP.
newsitem.headline: OVERNIGHT GUILDERS STEADY TO FIRM AFTER RECENT DIP.

text.p: Dutch guilders held largely steady in relatively brisk trade on Wednesday as one-day rates looked to be firming after dipping earlier this week.
Traders said most call money was changing hands at 2.93 percent, although some deals were also being done around 2.87 percent, the same as on Tuesday.
They said that after an initial adjustment, the market was taking the new-look cash reserve requirement in its stride.
Under the new arrangement introduced on May 23, banks with an end-of-day debit on their reserve account with the central bank are automatically topped up at the marginal advances rate.
Until now, this has encouraged banks to maintain a surplus, as the marginal advances rate is pegged at 4.5 percent.

But dealers said on Wednesday some players now seemed to be relaxing their stance, given that in some cases it would prove more economical to hold a small deficit than to maintain a positive balance as the latter received no interest.
Pointing to the central bank's weekly statement of accounts, they noted that commercial banks' reserves had fallen to 4.61 billion guilders on June 16 from an average 5.10 billion a week earlier.
The cash reserve requirement is currently set at 5.01 billion guilders and runs to June 23.
"This (change of attitude by the banks) is basically what's behind the fall in overnight rates," one dealer said.

But another dealer said rates were merely falling into line with their traditional benchmark under the "old" system, the special advances rate at which the central bank offers short-term liquidity. This is currently pegged at 2.9 percent.
"You can say why are call rates so low now, but equally you could be asking why they have been so high before," the dealer said.
He added: "The market seems to be coping quite well with the new cash reserve system."
Dealers said Wednesday's trade was concentrated at the short end, in guilders of up to one month.
One-month to one-year rates were unchanged across the board from Tuesday.
The guilder was quoting at 112.465 per 100 marks at around 1155 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday's 1215 GMT fixing.
